contactSheet.cameraNote: Rendered after the 3-D extent framing correction; the pre-correction tall-column renders were clipped and were not used for morphology review.

statusDefinitions.advance-candidate: The requested named feature is recognizable enough to justify a larger non-contact production candidate; this does not fill a catalog slot.
statusDefinitions.retune-candidate: The result is related but the defining named feature is weak, ambiguous, or overgrown; retain the route but change recipe, stop, or domain.
statusDefinitions.failed-probe: The defining named feature was not retained in this bounded run; the result cannot advance under this recipe.

reviews.rationale: The radius-2 three-layer seed overgrew into a decorated, branched thick plate and stopped on domain contact; it is not a small simple prism. Reuse the current fig11 candidate or stop much earlier on a larger domain.
Face and oblique views show a compact solid hexagonal column with no open axial cavity.
The long thin wall and open annular face remain visible; the form is distinct from the thicker hollow-column candidate.
The hooked seed grew into a complex six-armed plate and stopped on domain contact; no retained rolled or scroll-like plate edge is visible.
The asymmetric seed was overwhelmed by sixfold growth before domain contact; the final outline is hexagonal rather than a truncated triangle or threefold star.
The high-growth scale-down became a thick decorated plate and hit the boundary early; it is not a clean thin hexagonal plate baseline.
The end-on view shows a centered hollow region and the side view remains a slender symmetric column.
The recessed seed elongated into a nearly symmetric hollow column; it does not retain a one-ended cup profile.
Oblique structure is strongly three-dimensional and plate-bearing, but the central columns are visually crowded by secondary branches; compare a cleaner fig39/fig40-scale candidate.
The face view shows six broad thin star arms and a plate-like center; production needs a larger domain because this probe contacted the boundary.
The side view clearly shows two plate-like caps on opposite ends of a central column.
The face view retains two connected offset plate/star lobes rather than returning to one sixfold plate.
The compact hexagonal plate carries six prominent inward ridges/sectors and remains thin.
The side view shows an isolated tapered column with a pointed end, visually distinct from a uniform needle.
The alternating schedule produced end caps but no multiple separated cap levels; it remains visually one capped column.
The face view is open and branch-like but resembles a blocky stellar form; the named skeletal feature is ambiguous and needs a type-specific reference comparison.
Six arms are present, but broad secondary growth makes the result too ornate for a clean simple-star baseline.
The side view is a long slender columnar needle with little lateral decoration.
Two end caps are clear, but growth erased most of the tapered bullet distinction and the result reads primarily as a capped column.
The scale-down hit domain contact as a broad sectored/plate-like form without clear tree-like sidebranches; use the existing larger fig7/fig15 candidates.
The separated tips merged into one narrow axial envelope before domain contact; no readable cluster remains.
The oblique view is multilayered, but this small run does not clearly resolve one dominant plate plus a smaller nearby plate; retain the existing fig6 scientific anchor.
Numerous visible sidebranches give the six main branches a fern-like outline; production needs a larger domain because this probe contacted the boundary.
The annular seed filled and overgrew into a decorated hexagonal plate before domain contact; no stable hollow plate feature remains.
